headline: High: shared browser/MCP and file surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; compliance risk is elevated by secrets and mixed data classes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui ingests browser, MCP, OpenAPI, and file content, while TREK also uses browsers, WebSocket collaboration, and MCP. That creates a plausible default pathway for attacker-controlled content from one agent to be treated as instructions by the other. No provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF either agent forwards raw page or document text into the other's tool prompts without provenance tags, injection is reachable.
IF a shared MCP server or shared browser session is configured, cross-agent instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Route inter-agent content through a strict sanitizer that strips instructions.
Use separate browser profiles and cookies for each agent.
Add provenance labels to all imported text.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted tool schemas for cross-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles touch sensitive classes such as API keys, documents, reservations, MFA secrets, and persistent memory, and both expose files plus networked APIs. open-webui can access mounted data volumes and cloud APIs; TREK stores data in local DB/uploads/logs. A shared workspace or misrouted upload could leak secrets across the pair.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, uploaded files from one can be read by the other.
IF either agent is configured to send file contents to a third-party inference backend, sensitive data can leave the pair.
mitigations: Separate storage volumes for each agent.
Remove API keys and MFA secrets from shared folders.
Turn off automatic file upload to external inference endpoints.
Restrict logs to redacted metadata only.
requires-engineering: add per-agent encryption and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, subprocesses, and mounted-file access; TREK has allowlisted egress, browser use, MCP, and local DB/uploads/logs. Their write surfaces overlap on files and potentially shared mutable resources, so concurrent edits can conflict. The profiles do not show locking, so the interaction exists in default collaborative setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
IF both agents act on the same OAuth-backed resource, overlapping mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and databases.
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources.
Serialize tool actions through one orchestrator.
Use file locks or transaction boundaries.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate and route content through tools, while TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in and real-time actions over travel data. If TREK treats open-webui output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious suggestion can cascade into reservations, budgets, or itinerary changes. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF TREK consumes open-webui output without human review, erroneous actions can propagate.
IF open-webui is allowed to fabricate facts that TREK then renders or executes, downstream harm is reachable.
mitigations: Require human approval before bookings or edits.
Insert a verification step before TREK acts on external text.
Mark open-webui output as untrusted by default.
Limit automation to read-only suggestions.
requires-engineering: add citation and schema validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle regulated or sensitive data classes, but the profiles do not document a specific residency or certification mismatch. open-webui handles usage analytics, model evaluation data, and API keys; TREK handles reservations, email addresses, MFA secrets, and logs. The compliance risk is therefore a policy mismatch possibility rather than a proven breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed through a US-only backend without a DPA, residency risk appears.
IF retention settings differ between the agents for the same documents or logs, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Document data residency for both agents.
Align retention and deletion settings.
Exclude secrets from analytics and logs.
Review whether any regulated data is stored in uploads or mounted volumes.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for jurisdiction and retention.
